RITES Limited.desc: Indian engineering and transport consultancy working on railways, highways, metros, tunnels, bridges, airports and ports, and the export arm of Indian Railways for rolling stock including locomotives and coaches. A listed Government of India enterprise under the Ministry of Railways, incorporated on 26 April 1974, it says it has worked on more than 5,000 projects for clients in more than 55 countries.

sources.title: About Us

Ircon International Limited.desc: Indian construction company that builds railways, highways and bridges on a turnkey basis. It was set up by the Ministry of Railways in 1976 as Indian Railway Construction Company Limited, later renamed, and its shares were listed on the NSE and BSE in September 2018; its own site says turnover passed Rs 10,000 crore in 2023.

sources.title: Ircon International Limited (home and achievements)

Portos e Caminhos de Ferro de Mocambique.desc: Mozambique's state ports and railways company, a legal person of public law. A national ports and railways state company was created in 1989 and turned into a public company by Decree 40/94 of 13 September 1994; its 2010 corporate profile says it directly runs the southern railway lines to Ressano Garcia (88 km), Goba (74 km) and Limpopo (534 km), the port of Pemba and the fuel terminals in the ports of Maputo, Beira and Nacala, with the central and northern lines and the other port terminals held by concessionaires.

sources.title: CFM Corporate Profile
sources.publisher: Portos e Caminhos de Ferro de Mocambique, E.P. (CFM)

Organisation pour la Mise en Valeur du f.desc: Intergovernmental body that manages the Senegal River basin, set up by a convention adopted at Nouakchott on 11 March 1972 and signed that day by Mali, Mauritania and Senegal; Guinea joined later. Ownership of the works built under it is shared between the member states, and its High Commissioner wrote in 2014 that those works produce 800 GWh of electricity a year, that the irrigable potential is 375,000 hectares, and that they supply all the drinking water of Nouakchott and Saint-Louis and 60 per cent of Dakar's.

sources.title: Convention establishing the Senegal River Development Organization
L'Organisation pour la mise en valeur du fleuve Senegal montre l'exemple d'une gestion concertee de l'eau (post by the OMVS High Commissioner)

Société Nationale pour le Développement.desc: Mauritanian state body for irrigated farming, set up in 1975 as a public institution of a commercial and industrial nature with legal personality and financial independence. It takes part in planning and carrying out development policy along the Senegal River and its tributaries, monitors and maintains farm water infrastructure such as water channels, barriers and canals, and advises small farmers and collective irrigated farms and helps them obtain inputs.

sources.title: Presentation
sources.publisher: Societe Nationale pour le Developpement Rural (SONADER)

Nepal Intermodal Transport Development B.desc: Nepali government board set up under a 1998 formation order to develop, manage and promote the country's inland clearance depots, chaired by the secretary of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies. It leases out depot management to private firms chosen by competitive bidding, sets the criteria for terminal service charges, and makes rail cargo agreements with Indian Railways; Nepal's dry ports are at Birgunj, Biratnagar, Bhairahawa, Kakarbhitta and Tatopani.

sources.title: Nepal: country presentation on dry ports and intermodal transport

Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Suppl.desc: Nepali government ministry based at Singha Durbar in Kathmandu. Its four divisions cover administration, planning and monitoring; state institutions, supply management and consumer protection; bilateral and multilateral trade; and industrial investment promotion and industrial infrastructure development.

sources.title: Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies (official site)

Nepal Electricity Authority.desc: Nepal's state electricity utility. It began work on 16 August 1985 under the Nepal Electricity Authority Act 1984, formed by merging the Department of Electricity with the Nepal Electricity Corporation and several related development boards; it also recommends long- and short-term power plans to the government and proposes the electricity tariff, which needs government approval.

sources.title: About Us

Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and.desc: Nepali government ministry for physical infrastructure and transport. Four departments sit under it, for roads, transport management, railways and the Nepal Shipping Office, and its divisions include one for highways and alternative transport.

sources.title: Departments under the ministry
sources.publisher: Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport, Government of Nepal

National Highway Authority.desc: Pakistan's Economic Survey for 2024-25 says the Authority manages 48 national highways, motorways and strategic roads spanning 14,480 kilometres, and that it has led road infrastructure development in Pakistan.

sources.title: Pakistan Economic Survey, chapter on Transport and Communication
sources.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan

Land Revenue Departments of Khyber Pakht.desc: In Pakistan land use and ownership are provincial subjects, so land for a federal project is acquired by the province's revenue department, which deputes a land acquisition collector and revenue staff. The project's resettlement plan of 1 October 2007 names that department as the NWFP Revenue Department and says it may acquire private land or built-up property for public purposes, including on behalf of another provincial or federal agency.
Land Revenue Departments of Khyber Pakht.note: Filled by the checker from the project's own resettlement plan on disk (cache/P099040/RP_2007-10-01_8713349.txt, section 1.5.2), which the writer did not open. The plan describes only the provincial department, under the province's then name, the North-West Frontier Province; no opened source describes the Azad Jammu and Kashmir body, and kpbor.gov.pk is robots-disallowed to WebFetch.

sources.title: Resettlement Plan, Pakistan Earthquake Emergency Recovery Project, 1 October 2007 (project document on disk)

Electrocentro.desc: Peruvian electricity distribution company, legally Empresa Regional de Servicio Publico de Electricidad del Centro S.A., which buys power from generators and sells it in a concession area covering parts of Junin, Pasco, Ayacucho, Huanuco and Huancavelica and smaller areas in five other departments; it also runs transmission lines and some small hydro plants. The state holding company FONAFE owns all its shares, and it had 920,092 customers in November 2022.

sources.title: Informe de Transferencia de Gestion, Electrocentro S.A. (26.11.2022 al 10.12.2022)

Hidrandina.desc: Peruvian electricity distribution company serving La Libertad, Ancash and seven provinces of Cajamarca, with a concession area of about 8,570 square kilometres; it also runs public lighting and rural electrification work. It belongs to the Grupo Distriluz and the state holding company FONAFE holds more than 95 per cent of its capital. In 2024 it had 1,091,095 customers and 758 direct employees.

sources.title: Reporte de Sostenibilidad 2024

Dirección General de Electrificación Rur.desc: Unit of Peru's Ministry of Energy and Mines that develops rural electrification projects, created by Supreme Decree 026-2007-EM and working under the General Rural Electrification Law (Law 28749) and the regulation approved by Supreme Decree 018-2020-MINEM-DM. It coordinates with regional and local governments and with distribution and rural electrification concessionaires, and project formulation looks at current and 20-year demand, networks near the project area and social returns.

sources.title: Presentation to the Congress Energy and Mines Committee on rural electrification
sources.publisher: Ministerio de Energia y Minas / Congreso de la Republica del Peru

Manila Water Company, Inc..desc: Philippine water utility that treats and distributes water and provides sewerage and sanitation services in the East Zone of Metro Manila and Rizal province, covering 24 cities and towns over about 1,400 square kilometres and serving more than seven million people. It was incorporated in 1997, began operating in 2000, listed its shares in March 2005, and its own profile gives Trident Water as controlling shareholder with 52.16 per cent, alongside Philwater Holdings (19.01 per cent) and Ayala Corporation (12.26 per cent); its concession with MWSS runs to 2037.

sources.title: Business Profile

Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage Sys.desc: Philippine government corporation created by Republic Act 6234, approved on 19 June 1971, which abolished the National Waterworks and Sewerage Authority and took over its records, property, obligations and staff. Under that Act it owns and has jurisdiction over the waterworks and sewerage systems of the Metro Manila cities and nearby municipalities and parts of Rizal, Cavite and Bulacan, fixes water rates and sewerage service fees, and approves, regulates and supervises other waterworks and deepwells; since 1997 the water and sewerage operations in its two service zones have been run by private concessionaires under 25-year concessions.

sources.title: Republic Act No. 6234 (full text)
Our Company

Land Bank of the Philippines.desc: Philippine state bank, wholly owned by the national government, operating under Republic Act 3844 as last amended by Republic Act 10878. It runs commercial banking and uses those profits to finance its development programmes, with small farmers and fishers, many of them agrarian reform beneficiaries, among its priority sectors; its own site calls it by far the largest formal credit institution in rural areas and says it ranks among the country's top five commercial banks by deposits, assets and loans.

sources.title: Annual Corporate Governance Report 2024
About Us

Maynilad Water Services, Inc..desc: Philippine water utility supplying piped water, sewerage and septic-tank cleaning to the 17 cities and municipalities of the West Zone of Greater Metro Manila and to Kawit, Noveleta and Rosario in Cavite. It was granted a 25-year exclusive concession by the Philippine government in 1997, and a revised agreement executed on 18 May 2021 continues the concession to 31 July 2037; it is managed by Maynilad Water Holdings, a joint venture of Metro Pacific Investments, DMCI Holdings and Marubeni Corporation, whose consortium took control on 24 January 2007.

sources.title: Our Company

Dragonhart.note: The key gives only the single word 'Dragonhart', with no legal suffix. The project's own land acquisition report of May 2018 (cache/P113844/RP_2018-05-01_30330722.txt) names it once, as 'Dragonhart (the contractor)', and gives nothing else about the firm; that is the role the card already shows, not a description. Searches surfaced a Philippine firm, Dragonhart Construction Enterprise Inc., on job boards and a commercial database, but no page was opened tying that firm to this project. Blank confirmed by the checker.

National Irrigation Administration.desc: Philippine government-owned and controlled corporation responsible for the country's irrigation systems, created under Republic Act 3601 on 22 June 1963, its charter amended by Presidential Decree 552 on 11 September 1974 and Presidential Decree 1702 on 17 July 1980. Its 2024 annual report says it operated and maintained 262 national irrigation systems with an aggregate service area of 980,108 hectares, of which 876,565 hectares were firmed-up service area.

sources.title: Annual Report 2024

Laguna Lake Development Authority.desc: Philippine government body created by Republic Act 4850, approved on 18 July 1966, to promote and accelerate development of the Laguna Lake area. Under that Act the area covers the provinces of Rizal and Laguna and the cities of San Pablo, Manila, Pasay, Quezon and Caloocan; the Authority drafts the area's development plan for national planning approval, approves or disapproves projects there, has exclusive power to issue new permits for use of the lake waters, including navigation and fishpens, acts with other agencies in setting water quality standards for waste discharged into the lake, and may finance and undertake infrastructure works.

sources.title: Republic Act No. 4850 (full text)
sources.publisher: Asian Development Bank, Law and Policy Reform

Municipal Government of Rodriguez, Rizal.desc: Local government of Rodriguez, also known as Montalban, a municipality in Rizal province in the Calabarzon region of the Philippines. The 2020 census counted 443,954 residents, seventh among the region's cities and municipalities.

sources.title: 2020 Census of Population and Housing, Region IV-A press release

Regional Authority for Water Management.desc: Polish state water management body seated in Gliwice. Since 1 January 2018 it has been one of eleven regional water management boards of Panstwowe Gospodarstwo Wodne Wody Polskie, with the Mala Wisla, Upper Odra and Czadeczka water regions in its charge; the boards carry out duties under the water law, give opinions on plans and decisions, and their directors act as the economic regulator for water supply and sewerage.

sources.title: Rozporzadzenie nadajace statut Panstwowemu Gospodarstwu Wodnemu Wody Polskie (Dz.U. 2017 poz. 2506)
Rozporzadzenie w sprawie wlasciwosci miejscowej dyrektorow regionalnych zarzadow gospodarki wodnej Wod Polskich (Dz.U. 2018 poz. 510)

Lower Silesian Board for Amelioration an.desc: Polish public body based in Wroclaw, a local-government budget unit whose stated field of work, in a contract award notice of March 2017, was the tasks of building and maintaining waters and water structures laid down by the water law. Under the new Water Law in force from 1 January 2018, the state body Panstwowe Gospodarstwo Wodne Wody Polskie carries out the water-maintenance tasks of the voivodeship marshals.

sources.title: Contract award notice 106898-2017, Dolnoslaski Zarzad Melioracji i Urzadzen Wodnych we Wroclawiu
Nowe Prawo wodne - informacje dla gmin po szkoleniu
sources.publisher: Zwiazek Gmin i Powiatow Subregionu Centralnego Wojewodztwa Slaskiego

Palestinian Energy and Natural Resources.desc: Palestinian Authority body for the energy sector. A legal record of Decree-Law 13 of 2009, the General Electricity Law, says Article 4 gives it policy development, international cooperation, safety enforcement, issuing codes, tariff setting and licensing of energy projects, all requiring approval from the Council of Ministers; the same record says generation and distribution licences cannot be transferred without its prior approval and that it is charged with advancing research on renewable energy.

sources.title: Decree-Law No. 13 (2009) regarding the General Electricity Law
sources.publisher: UNEP Law and Environment Assistance Platform (FAOLEX record)

Israel Electric Corporation.desc: Israel's main electricity company, working across generation, transmission, distribution and supply; its 2025 investor presentation says it focuses on transmission and distribution and has reduced its share of generation. The State of Israel holds 99.85 per cent of its shares, and the presentation gives 3.0 million customers at 31 December 2024 and revenue of ILS 26,184 million for 2024.

sources.title: Investors Presentation 2025

Electrogaz.desc: Rwanda's former state water and electricity utility. It was founded in 1939 as REGIDESO, split into Rwandan and Burundian arms in 1963, and renamed Electrogaz in 1976 with a monopoly on producing and distributing water and electricity. A law of 9 September 2008 divided it into the Rwanda Energy Company (RECO) and the Rwanda Water and Sanitation Company (RWASCO); those two were merged in 2010 into the Energy, Water and Sanitation Authority, which was itself unbundled in 2014 into Rwanda Energy Group Limited and the Water and Sanitation Corporation.

sources.title: History
History

Energy Water and Sanitation Authority, R.desc: Rwanda's former state utility for electricity, water and sanitation, created in 2010 by merging the Rwanda Energy Company and the Rwanda Water and Sanitation Company, which had been split off from Electrogaz in 2008. The law repealing the law that established it is dated 31 January 2014; the two successor companies, Rwanda Energy Group Limited and the Water and Sanitation Corporation, were incorporated in July 2014 with 100 per cent government shareholding, and a Prime Minister's Order of 16 August 2014 set the terms for transferring its property and responsibilities.

sources.title: History
History

Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resou.desc: Rwandan government ministry for farming and livestock, which aims at sustainable development of a modern, efficient and competitive agriculture and livestock sector and at food security, agricultural exports and diversification of production, under the National Agricultural Policy (2018) and the fifth Strategic Plan for the Transformation of Agriculture. Its directorates general cover planning, agriculture modernisation, animal resources development, and agriculture value chain management and trade.

sources.title: About the Ministry
sources.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources, Republic of Rwanda

Companhia Santomense de Telecomunicações.desc: Telecommunications operator in Sao Tome and Principe, founded in 1990, which builds, installs and maintains fixed and mobile networks and sells fixed and mobile service to households and businesses. In February 2022 the Portuguese group Visabeira Global agreed to buy the 51 per cent stake held by Africatel, a Dutch holding controlled by Brazil's Oi, with the state of Sao Tome and Principe keeping 49 per cent; a Visabeira release in 2025 describes the company as held by Grupo Visabeira and the Santomean state.

sources.title: Visabeira buys 51% of telecoms operator CST
Companhia Santomense de Telecomunicacoes - 35 anos (press release)

Agência Fiduciária de Administração de P.desc: Agency in Sao Tome and Principe that administers donor-funded projects, represented by its general director. It signs World Bank grant agreements as the project implementing entity, and under them it is responsible for disbursement, monitoring and evaluation and reporting, for having its financial statements audited each year, and for running a grievance mechanism, which includes a free telephone line.

sources.title: Project Agreement for Additional Financing Grant D778-ST
Implementation status report, Sao Tome and Principe Institutional Capacity Building project

BOTAS Petroleum Pipeline Corporation.desc: Turkish state oil and gas company, in full Boru Hatlari ile Petrol Tasima Anonim Sirketi, which moves petroleum by pipeline and runs gas transmission, trading and storage, and which publishes tariffs for crude oil, natural gas and port services. Turkey's state audit office lists it first among the 25 state economic enterprises subject to Decree-Law 233 and puts its current assets at about 506 billion lira at the end of 2023.

sources.title: 2023 yili Kamu Isletmeleri Genel Raporu
About Us

State Road Agency of Ukraine (Ukravtodor.desc: Ukraine's former national roads body. In January 2023 it was folded into a new central executive body, the State Agency for Restoration and Infrastructure Development, formed on the foundation of Ukravtodor and Ukrinfraproekt, which carries out state policy on road infrastructure and also builds, reconstructs and repairs housing, social, transport and energy infrastructure and border crossing points, directed and coordinated through the minister for recovery, infrastructure and transport.

sources.title: About the Agency
sources.publisher: State Agency for Restoration and Infrastructure Development of Ukraine

Bukhara Regional Production State Enterp.desc: Water and sewerage utility for the Bukhara region of Uzbekistan, named in World Bank papers as the Bukhara Regional Production Enterprise Suvokova and as one of 14 regional unitary enterprise Suvokovas set up in a sector reform. It was the Bukhara implementing agency for the rehabilitation of the city's wastewater treatment plant and sewer network, with 34 km of sewers replaced and 12.4 km newly built as of 30 November 2020. A presidential decree reported in November 2019 converted the state unitary water supply enterprises in housing and communal services into limited liability companies and created the joint-stock company Uzsuvtaminot; a 2025 tender for Bukhara region water supply and sewerage works names JSC Bukhara Suv Taminoti as the purchaser.

sources.title: Disclosable Restructuring Paper, Uzbekistan Bukhara and Samarkand Sewerage Project (P112719)
Implementation Status and Results Report, Bukhara and Samarkand Sewerage Project, Sequence No. 20
Unitarnye predpriyatiya vodosnabzheniya preobrazovyvayutsya v obshchestva s ogranichennoy otvetstvennostyu
Specific Procurement Notice, Bukhara Region Water Supply and Sewerage Project Phase 1

Projects Implementation Unit for Water I.desc: Uzbek government unit that runs donor-financed irrigation and drainage projects, working alongside construction supervision and monitoring consultants. World Bank reporting from 2021 names it the Project Implementation Unit under the Ministry of Water of Uzbekistan and records it designing the criteria for choosing the farmers who host demonstration plots. The Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources was reported in February 2018 to have been split into a Ministry of Agriculture and a Ministry of Water Resources.

sources.title: Implementation Status and Results Report, Ferghana Valley Water Resources Management Phase II (P149610), Sequence No. 09
Uzbek agriculture and water resources ministry split into two

Ministry of Transport, Works, Urban Deve.desc: Government ministry of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. A gazette of 10 November 2017 assigning ministerial responsibilities under the 1979 constitution gave it roads and traffic, sea and river defences, public buildings and works, the electrical inspectorate, urban development, local government and postal services.

sources.title: Extraordinary Gazette No. 59 of 2017, assignment of ministerial responsibilities
sources.publisher: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

Central Planning Division, Ministry of F.desc: Unit inside Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning. The operations manual of November 2014 for a World Bank-financed disaster vulnerability project names it the project's main coordinating body, responsible for procurement, processing disbursement documents, financial management, monitoring the project's result indicators and managing environmental and social safeguards, relying on the participating line ministries for technical support. In the gazette of 10 November 2017 the economic planning portfolio sits with the Minister of Finance, Economic Planning, Sustainable Development and Information Technology.

sources.title: Regional Disaster Vulnerability Reduction Project, Operations Manual (November 2014)
sources.publisher: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

sources.title: Extraordinary Gazette No. 59 of 2017, assignment of ministerial responsibilities
sources.publisher: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

Korporata Energjetike e Kosoves (KEK).desc: Kosovo's state-owned electricity producer, which runs the lignite-fired Kosovo A and Kosovo B power stations; the district heating company Termokos heats Pristina with cogeneration at Kosovo B. Over 90 per cent of Kosovo's electricity is generated from coal at those two plants.

sources.title: Energy prices and subsidies in Kosovo, in Energy Prices and Subsidies in the Western Balkans
Prime Minister Kurti and Minister Rizvanolli visit the Kosovo Energy Corporation
sources.publisher: Ministry of Economy, Republic of Kosovo

Ministry of Environment and Spatial Plan.desc: Kosovo government ministry for the environment and spatial planning, among the institutions re-established after 2000. In the 2021 state of the environment report it appears under the wider name Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure, which proposes that annual report to the government, and whose inspectorate carried out about 200 inspections of river sand and gravel extraction between 2019 and 2021, leading to 118 decisions prohibiting works, 7 criminal charges, 24 minor offence reports and 93 fines.

sources.title: Report on the State of the Environment 2021

rePlan Inc..desc: Canadian consulting firm based in Toronto and founded in 1978, which advised natural resource and infrastructure companies and financial institutions on social impact and risk. The environmental consultancy ERM announced on 11 August 2015 that it had bought the business, which the trade press reports under the name rePlan.

sources.title: ERM acquires Canadian social impact and risk specialist

Road Development Agency, Zambia.desc: Zambian government agency responsible for the care, maintenance and construction of public roads, established by the Public Roads Act No. 12 of 2002 as amended by Act No. 9 of 2022 and operating since 2006; it also regulates the maximum weights permitted on roads and administers the National Road Tolling Programme under the Tolls Act No. 14 of 2011. Its 2022 annual report puts the entire classified road network in its charge at 67,671 km, with its efforts focused on a rationalised core road network of 40,454 km.

sources.title: Annual Report 2022
